analysis.title: Global Rates Trader: AI Volatility Disrupts Energy Risks
key_insights: GS keeps a long-duration bias anchored in the belly of the US curve. The recent rally narrowed the gap between long-term US yields and fair value, but underweight positioning, smaller technical risks and risk-asset pressure from higher yields remain in place.

Duration worked as a hedge when AI worries drove risk-off. GS says this is consistent with some durability in the compression of term premium, though some reversal of the rally is possible if risk-off fades and energy prices keep rising.

An on-hold decision is expected at next week's FOMC. Market pricing through mid-2027 is roughly an every-other-meeting hike pace, and the Committee's relative emphasis on inflation versus tighter financial conditions will set how sticky very front-end pricing is.

GS prefers belly outperformance as a bullish-leaning expression because belly longs typically do relatively better through rate hikes and their aftermath, even though the valuation asymmetry has moderated.

Midterm elections are a possible source of post-FOMC volatility. GS expects the initial rates reaction to depend on perceived implications for AI regulation and on Iran conflict developments, more than on fiscal policy. A shift in the AI investment trajectory would likely dominate as a driver of duration.

Implied rates vol skewed toward lower yields this week. For the first time since the summer lows, the cost of lower-yield (left tail) protection rose meaningfully versus upside protection. The implied vol surface peaks at the 1y1y point.

GS still sees value in selling high strikes, either outright or to finance lower-yield protection, using the premium buildup in 1y1y or exposure in the belly. Vol is expected to move counter to yields in the short term: a reversal in yields on easing AI fears could bring a gradual vol decline, while deeper growth concerns are the clearest route to a further rise.

GS favors real rate longs over nominals in the US because fading inflation pressures in 2027 should give more relief in hawkish policy pricing and real rates. The main risk to this is growth-led disinflation, which typically favors nominal longs.

US inflation pricing is broadly in line with GS forecasts and fair value. In Europe it looks elevated versus forecasts and on the high side of fair value, especially in near-dated forwards, so GS prefers near-dated nominal forwards such as 1y1y or 1y2y there.
Breakevens tightened this week after controlling for oil, consistent with their positive correlation to AI-related sentiment.

BoC: despite a benign September inflation report, Macklem signaled the inflation outlook at next week's meeting will be 'quite a bit higher'. GS economists expect hikes in October and January, but see market pricing of two further hikes after that as too much given sub-2% trim and median inflation, trade tensions and a subdued labor market. GS prefers CAD belly longs, since the CAD curve is the steepest among peers.

ECB: GS expects a measured tone and an on-hold decision at next week's meeting. A message that sounds relaxed about sovereign stress is a risk to the very front end (through Mar-27), since December is not fully priced. The link between hawkish policy risk and sovereign spread volatility should limit how far Z7 can sell off.
GS continues to like Euro area curve flatteners such as 2s5s into the winter.

French OATs trade more than 60bps cheap to fair value, even allowing for non-linearities. GS expects any spread tightening to be staggered, with elections and deficit reduction the key catalysts. Energy relief would help via lower core yields and volatility.
GS raised mid-2027 10y spread forecasts to OAT-Bund 130bps (from 95), BTP-Bund 105bps (from 90) and Bonos-Bund 55bps (unchanged).

GS sees limited risk of a UK 2022-style self-reinforcing sell-off through the domestic financial sector. DB pension fund assets are below 1% of GDP in France and Italy, euro area banks are better capitalized, and insurers see sovereign spread widening as a manageable headwind.

UK Budget: GS expects changes to be about maturity mix, not size. It forecasts a £5bn rise in the central government net cash requirement financed through bills, lifting net bill supply from £5bn to £10bn. Planned Gilt sales stay at £246.2bn, skewed shorter and with fewer long conventional and linker sales.

GS favors Gilts versus swaps over outright duration, and sees owning 10y Gilts on asset swap as favorable given the improving supply backdrop. Strong growth, a firmer labor market and energy pressures keep the domestic macro backdrop challenging.

Japan: the long end of the JGB curve is more stable, with lifers still buying long and super-long JGBs in September. 10s30s looks slightly flat to fair value while 2s5s and 5s10s remain steeper than fair. GS expects the BoJ to hold at its upcoming meeting and keeps the 5y sector as its preferred underweight on the JPY curve.

Australia: GS economists now expect a final RBA hike in November before easing begins in 2H27. Market pricing for November is only 14bps. GS keeps its preference for front-end flatteners and tightened the stop on its IRZ6U7 flattener to 7bp.

New Zealand: GS economists added a hike in October followed by a final hike in December. GS still sees cumulative hike pricing as excessive given slack, and sees dovish spillovers from abroad as the clearest route to lower NZD yields.
GS 10y yield forecasts: USD spot 4.98% with 4.75% at 4Q26 and 4.40% at 4Q27, versus spot of 3.34% for Germany, 5.07% France, 4.59% Italy, 5.35% UK and 2.81% Japan.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS expects a hold amid still-present inflation pressure and tighter financial conditions. Market pricing through mid-2027 is roughly an every-other-meeting hike pace.
GS economists expect two hikes, which would put the policy rate mid-way in the BoC's neutral range. Market pricing of two further hikes after that looks excessive to GS.
GS expects a measured tone. A message relaxed about sovereign stress could pressure the very front end through Mar-27.

macro_indicators.reading: Final hike in November, easing from 2H27
macro_indicators.interpretation: Market pricing for November is only 14bps, and GS expects hike expectations to be very front loaded.

macro_indicators.reading: Hike in October, final hike in December
macro_indicators.interpretation: Rising oil prices, a weaker NZD and broader inflation pressure in 3Q26 raised the odds of earlier hikes. GS sees cumulative pricing as excessive given slack.
GS expects no signal of increased inflation-overshoot risk. Market pricing assumes more tightening than GS's base case, which weighs on the belly more than the long end.

macro_indicators.indicator: UK central government net cash requirement
macro_indicators.interpretation: Expected to be financed through bills, lifting net bill supply from £5bn to £10bn with planned Gilt sales unchanged at £246.2bn.
GS forecasts 4.65% at 1Q27, 4.55% at 2Q27, 4.45% at 3Q27 and 4.40% at 4Q27.

trade_ideas.description: Long belly of the US curve for outperformance (bullish-leaning belly expression)
trade_ideas.rationale: Belly longs typically perform relatively better through rate hikes and the immediate aftermath.
trade_ideas.risk: A reversal of the rate rally if risk-off moderates and energy prices keep rising.

trade_ideas.description: Sell high-strike rates options outright or to finance lower-yield protection, using 1y1y premium or belly exposure
trade_ideas.rationale: Premium has built up in 1y1y and the vol surface peaks there.
trade_ideas.risk: Deeper growth concerns could push vol higher.

trade_ideas.description: Long US real rates versus nominals
trade_ideas.rationale: Fading inflation pressure should give more relief in hawkish policy pricing and real rates in the US.
trade_ideas.risk: Growth-led disinflation, which typically favors nominal longs.

trade_ideas.description: Long near-dated EUR nominal forwards such as 1y1y or 1y2y
trade_ideas.rationale: European inflation pricing is rich versus GS forecasts and fair value, so near-dated forwards capture less hawkish policy expectations as inflation risks ease.
Feedback between hawkish ECB risk and sovereign credit volatility limits front-end selloffs, and points further out should benefit.
trade_ideas.risk: A relaxed ECB message on sovereign stress could pressure the very front end.

trade_ideas.description: Long 10y Gilts on asset swap (Gilts versus swaps)
trade_ideas.rationale: Easing net duration supply from a shorter-skewed remit should help swap spreads, and the 10y ASW recovery has lagged what supply implies.
trade_ideas.risk: Material fiscal slippage at the Budget or a tougher spending review next year.

trade_ideas.description: Underweight the 5y sector of the JPY curve, with flattening pressure
trade_ideas.rationale: Market concern that more BoJ tightening is needed weighs on the belly more than the long end.
trade_ideas.risk: More deliberate BoJ messaging favors this pattern, while a faster hike path is not a stated risk.

trade_ideas.description: AUD front-end flatteners (IRZ6U7), stop tightened to 7bp
trade_ideas.rationale: Hike expectations should be front loaded, and relief would reassess the terminal rate.
The CAD curve is the steepest among peers and a reduction in front-end hike premium could lower yields. Treasuries' hedge role against AI wobbles also helps.

risk_factors: A reversal of the rate rally if risk-off moderates and energy prices keep rising.
More persistent inflation could limit dovish repricing.
Growth-led disinflation would favor nominal longs over real rate longs.
A relaxed ECB message on sovereign stress could pressure the very front end (through Mar-27).
French and Italian political and fiscal risk, including elections, social unrest and budget negotiations.
Fiscal challenges beyond the UK Budget, including a tougher spending review next year, could limit long-end Gilt risk premia compression.
Midterm elections, AI regulation and Iran conflict developments as post-FOMC volatility sources.
CORRA pressures around the Canadian banks' financial year end.
JGB fiscal concerns could be reignited and break the supportive demand backdrop.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 plots 3m TU 25-delta call/put implied vol, showing downside yield protection has become more expensive relative to upside recently.
Exhibit 2 plots the GS US Broad AI Index against 10y breakevens residual to oil, showing breakevens tightened during this week's risk-off.
Exhibit 4 shows OATs trading more than 60bps cheap to fair value, averaged over 5 specifications.
Exhibit 5 compares DB pension fund, bank and insurer sizes and domestic government bond holdings for France, Italy and the euro area.
Exhibit 6 shows 2026/27 Gilt supply unchanged but skewed toward shorter maturities versus the April 2026 remit and the 2012-25 average.
vol_and_positioning: The cost of lower-yield protection (3m TU 25-delta) rose meaningfully versus upside protection this week, the first time since the summer lows.
The implied rates vol surface peaks at 1y1y because uncertainty around the terminal rate remains high.
GS sees value in selling high strikes outright or to finance lower-yield protection, using 1y1y premium or belly exposure.
Vol is expected to move counter to yields short term. Easing AI fears could bring a gradual vol decline, while deeper growth concerns would push it higher.
GS fund positioning indicator current score is -3, option implied position indicator is 0, and data response indicator is -1.

CFTC duration-weighted spec net positions are negative across SFR (-74.2), TU (-30.8), FV (-45.0), TY (-58.6), TN (-17.1), US (-17.7) and WN (-49.0) $mm/bp. Asset managers and others are net long in TU, FV, TY, TN, US and WN.
GS describes duration positioning as underweight, one of the factors it cites for a constructive duration tilt.
geopolitical: Iran conflict developments around the midterm elections could affect the initial rates market reaction.
French social unrest and ongoing budget negotiations are cited as obstacles to a return of OAT valuations to fundamentals.
Trade tensions are cited as a limit on how far the BoC hikes.

tension_points.bull_case: Duration proved its hedge value when AI worries drove risk-off, and underweight positioning, smaller technical risks and risk-asset pressure from higher yields remain, which supports some durability in term premium compression.
tension_points.bear_case: The rally has compressed the valuation gap, and a reversal is possible if risk-off tone moderates and energy prices keep rising.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A moderation of the risk-off tone combined with persistent energy price increases.

tension_points.bull_case: Feedback between hawkish ECB risk and sovereign spread volatility imposes a speed limit on how far Z7 can sell off, which supports 2s5s flatteners.
tension_points.bear_case: A relaxed message on sovereign stress could push the very front end higher through Mar-27, since December is not fully priced.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A signal from the ECB that more stress is needed before intervention, which lets the very front end converge toward pricing implied by energy pressures alone.

tension_points.bull_case: Fading inflation pressure in 2027 should give more relief in hawkish policy pricing and real rates in the US.
tension_points.bear_case: Growth-led disinflation typically sees nominal longs clearly outperform real rate longs.
